item.title: Big Tech and green groups meet to discuss the future of data centres in the US
item.description: As artificial intelligence drives demand for more data centres, some of the world's biggest technology companies are joining forces with environmental groups to address concerns over their impact on local communities in the United States.

item.title: EU prosecutors probe fraud claims over funds for Spanish rail line hit by deadly crash
item.description: EU prosecutors have opened a fraud investigation into funds for upgrading Spain’s Madrid–Seville high-speed line, where a 28 October crash near Urda killed 69. A similar probe began in March after a January crash on the same line killed 46.

item.title: Japan: Commuters flock to see two goats grazing at Tokyo station
item.description: Two white goats have become unlikely celebrities in central Tokyo after being recruited to clear overgrown vegetation near Yotsuya railway station. Their eco-friendly gardening duties are attracting crowds of delighted onlookers.

item.title: Hormuz standoff ‘not sustainable’, senior Iranian lawmaker tells Euronews
item.description: MP and foreign minister under Ahmadinejad, Manouchehr Mottaki, told Euronews that multiple ships a day were being disabled as the IRGC Navy worked to bring unauthorised transit to zero. He called on Washington to lift its naval blockade strangling the Iranian economy before talks resume.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 6th, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 6th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: EU and UK set to link carbon markets in major post-Brexit deal
item.description: The agreement to link EU and UK carbon markets, expected to be announced at the 20 November summit, could spare manufacturers additional carbon border charges, but critics warn that closer alignment could drive up costs for British industry.

item.title: Irish media outlets evacuate staff in Dublin following bomb threats
item.description: It comes amid a flurry of bomb hoaxes targeting European airlines and around a week before Dublin is due to host a meeting of the European Political Community.

item.title: Bomb threat targets Ryanair flight to Lisbon as scares continue across Europe
item.description: The Ryanair flight, which was travelling from Rome to Lisbon, landed at around 8 am this morning, prompting the authorities to take action.

item.title: Emergency services deployed after school bus crash kills two in France
item.description: A minor and a young adult were killed when a bus carrying pupils crashed in eastern France on Friday morning. Emergency services deployed helicopters to the scene as authorities launched an investigation into the circumstances.

item.title: Exclusive: US is 'playing politics' with Patriot missiles - Finnish minister
item.description: Finnish Defence Minister Antti Häkkänen tells Euronews that European allies have already paid for the Patriot interceptor missiles, but Washington has yet to approve their delivery as Ukraine braces for further Russian attacks on its energy infrastructure.

item.title: 'An insult to his culture': Italian chef loses job after refusing to put pineapple on pizza
item.description: Chef Davide Tamburella refused to put the tropical fruit on pizzas at a restaurant in Brisbane, Australia, calling it "an insult to his culture". Having been fired from his job, he has lost his legal battle against the establishment.

item.title: Inside the EU’s battle to bar Russian war veterans from Europe
item.description: Ukraine has shared the names of more than half a million Russian soldiers, but fewer than 1% have been added to the EU’s Schengen security database. Brussels is now exploring ways to overcome the legal hurdles amid growing concerns over Russian security threats.

item.title: Europe's climate tax risks opening a new trade war with India at COP31
item.description: The EU's diplomatic stance at COP31 summit is complicated by its own political retreat on climate policy and growing global opposition to its carbon border tax.

item.title: Poland warns allies: Don't negotiate with Russia over Eastern Europe's head
item.description: Poland has warned that Eastern Europe's security interests must not be sidelined in negotiations to end the war in Ukraine, as it pushes back against efforts to resume Russian gas imports.

item.title: Judge blocks construction of Trump's massive 'triumphal arch'
item.description: Trump has said the structure would be turned into a "top grade military complex" housing drones, snipers and ammunition.

item.title: Grizzly bear hunt underway after mother and daughter killed in Canada
item.description: A mother and her daughter have been found dead following a suspected bear attack near Bella Coola, in British Columbia. Conservation officers say multiple grizzlies may have been involved, with trapping efforts underway. Authorities have imposed a curfew as the investigation continues.

item.title: Google, Meta and TikTok sue California to block law protecting kids from social media harms
item.description: The Big Tech companies have filed separate lawsuits to block a California law aimed at protecting children under-16 from harmful social media features such as endless scrolling and addictive feeds, which goes into force 1 January 2027.

item.title: Paraguay: Thousands protest banking scandal as president faces impeachment
item.description: Thousands of Paraguayans have taken to the streets over a banking scandal that has left nearly half the population without access to their savings. Protesters are demanding President Santiago Peña face impeachment despite his offer to resign.

item.title: This Greek ship has collected enough waste from remote shorelines to fill 22 Olympic swimming pools
item.description: The 20-member cleaning team has created the largest database on marine pollution in the Mediterranean.

item.title: 'Weaponising disruption.' Travel expert Eoghan Corry comments on recent European hoax bomb threats
item.description:
"Nobody really has a chance of getting a bomb onboard... you've got to remember how safe European airspace is."
Eoghan Corry, editor of Travel Extra, speaks to Euronews on the recent hoax bomb threats affecting multiple European airlines on Tuesday.

item.title: 'Biggest wave' in 50 years, says US political analyst Bruce Stokes on US midterm election results
item.description: "We have a long saying in the United States: it's the economy, stupid." Stefan Grobe speaks to Bruce Stokes, a Senior Fellow at the German Marshall Fund, on the recent US midterm election results.

item.title: One killed and three injured in strikes on Ukraine as blaze reported at Russia's Afipsky oil refinery
item.description: Ukrainian authorities said on Friday that one man had been killed in a morning attack on the Rivne region. Three others were also reportedly injured in strikes on Kyiv Oblast overnight.

item.title: 'Political willingness' from the US needed to start sending Patriot missiles to Ukraine
item.description: Finnish Defence Minister Antti Häkkänen said that as now Europeans are the "biggest supporter" for Ukraine, the continent can't show exhaustion as it "weakens the negoitation position."

item.title: Cracks emerge over Europe’s fragmented approach to Ukraine peace talks
item.description: Good morning. I’m Mared Gwyn, holding the newsletter pen again this Friday. In this edition: Meloni takes Brussels to task over its Ukraine peace strategy, and the European Commission is set to unveil its annual migration check-up.

item.title: Euronews Culture's Film of the Week: 'Wild Horse Nine' – Guns, coups, and suicidal birds
item.description: Essentially a companion piece to McDonagh's debut 'In Bruges', 'Wild Horse Nine' can feel like familiar ground. However, John Malkovich makes every acerbic, funny and at times surprisingly moving line of dialogue a joy to watch, and he's a shoo-in for Best Actor at next year's Oscars.

item.title: Audio reveals moment Ryanair pilots are told military aircraft is intercepting them
item.description: A Ryanair flight from London Stansted to Sofia was diverted to Plovdiv, Bulgaria, after a reported bomb threat on board. Air traffic controllers warned the pilots that a military aircraft was intercepting them as they entered Bulgarian airspace.

item.title: Europe Today: Trump weighs Iran strikes as Ukraine talks head to Abu Dhabi
item.description: With the midterms over, attention turns to Donald Trump's next move on Iran, as US officials reportedly warn Gulf allies to prepare for new strikes. Ukraine talks head to Abu Dhabi next week. We also look at the wave of bomb threats on European flights and a new book on Emmanuel Macron.

item.title: European stocks join global rout after worst US chip sell-off since 2020
item.description: S&P 500 companies lost a record $2.9 trillion (€2.6 trillion) in market value on Thursday. European shares opened lower on Friday as investors weighed whether Democrats’ US midterm wins could lead to tougher rules on AI data centres.

item.title: COP31 host Türkiye is home to one of Europe's largest solar farms. Why can’t it kick coal?
item.description: As Türkiye prepares to host the UN climate summit, one critic describes the country's climate targets and policies as “critically insufficient”.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 6th, 2026 – Morning
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 6th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: Kerala beyond the backwaters: Why you should book an ayurvedic-led wellness stay in 2027
item.description: The Indian state is encouraging visitors to discover ayurveda on their next visit, and to also come for Onam, a traditional harvest festival in September.

item.title: UK tax havens linked to €8bn in EU tax losses: Who loses most?
item.description: EU countries lose nearly €60bn a year to corporate profit shifting, the Tax Justice Network estimates. It links about €8bn of those losses to the UK and its tax haven network, even as the UK itself ranks among the countries that lose the most worldwide.

item.title: Zelenskyy urges Latin American leaders to help repair Ukraine's power grid
item.description: Speaking at the Ibero-American Summit in Madrid, Zelenskyy urged leaders to help Ukraine obtain the necessary equipment to repair its power grid that got damaged from Russian attacks.

item.title: West Bank: Palestinians harvest olives under Israeli military restrictions
item.description: Palestinian farmers in the occupied West Bank have been allowed limited access to their olive groves under Israeli military restrictions. Many found damaged trees, while soldiers fired tear gas near the harvest.

item.title: Spain: Zelensky urges Latin America to help repair Ukraine's power grid
item.description: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky has appealed to Spain and Latin American countries for urgent help repairing Ukraine's damaged energy infrastructure. He also met King Felipe VI during the Ibero-American Summit in Madrid.

item.title: Paraguayan president resigns amid bank collapse leaving 3M people without access to bank accounts
item.description: Santiago Peña resigned as president of Paraguay amid the Ueno Bank crisis and was later impeached over an alleged conflict of interest. Vice President Pedro Alliana will take office, while millions of Paraguayans wait to recover their deposits.

item.title: British comedian Russell Brand found guilty of rape and three sexual assaults by London jury
item.description: Russell Brand was convicted of four sexual offences, one rape and three sexual assaults, involving four women between 2005 and 2009 in different locations.

item.title: Greece: Students march in Athens demanding more education funding
item.description: Thousands of pupils, students and teachers marched through central Athens on Thursday in a nationwide push for better-funded schools, joining a protest wave that has spread from France across southern Europe.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | November 5th, 2026 – Evening
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this November 5th, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: World Investment Forum in Doha examines what attracts investment and what holds it back
item.description: Foreign investment remains concentrated in relatively few countries, while others struggle to attract funding. At the World Investment Forum in Doha, governments and businesses discussed how more economies could benefit and turn investment into jobs.

item.title: Putin seizes Russian operations of cigarette giant Japan Tobacco International
item.description: The decree transferred JTI’s four factories, around 4,000 employees and roughly 40% of the Russian cigarette market to a state-linked holding company. The latest seizure added to a list that includes Nestlé, Auchan, Leroy Merlin and Metro.

item.title: Everyday people: Jeans, plastic and paper among Met Gala's surprising new fashion themes
item.description: The 2027 Met Gala will celebrate the potential of everyday objects and materials, from jeans and T-shirts to paper and plastic. The accompanying exhibition next spring will explore how designers transform ordinary items into works of art.

item.title: EU plans to deliver 'AI literacy' certificates to students
item.description: The European Union has announced that it has started to work on creating a certificate for "AI literacy" that would be delivered to successful 15-year-old students for the next school year.

item.title: Italian PM slams EU’s fragmented approach to Ukraine peace talks
item.description: In a letter to European Council President António Costa, Giorgia Meloni says multiple negotiating formats are making Europe “less credible” to end the war.

item.title: Protesters across Europe to call for freeze on energy hungry data centres
item.description: After US midterms, European campaigners bring the data centre backlash to Europe.

item.title: Fireworks may be fun, but their health risks are not
item.description: Fireworks may be a staple of celebrations, but their health risks are prompting experts to call for stricter regulations and greater public awareness.

item.title: Ueno Bank collapse in Paraguay prompts President Santiago Peña to resign
item.description: The accounting black hole at Ueno Bank wipes out public funds, leaves thousands without access to their deposits and drives Paraguay into its worst institutional crisis in years.

item.title: France: Up to 55,000 march in Lyon amid clashes and tear gas
item.description: Tens of thousands marched through Lyon area during a nationwide strike over wages and purchasing power. Police charged demonstrators and used tear gas as clashes erupted along the protest route.

item.title: More flights, fewer emissions: this country’s aviation challenge
item.description: Azerbaijan is working to reduce aviation emissions while handling growing air traffic. From fuel-efficient aircraft and airport carbon accreditation to digital air navigation, the industry is exploring ways to make flying more sustainable.

item.title: Inside New Tashkent, Uzbekistan's planned city for two million people
item.description: Nearly 7,000 apartments are complete, three ministries already operate there and university facilities have opened. Projects worth $50bn (€44.8bn) are planned for the first phase, with a FIFA-standard stadium under construction and a metro connection proposed.
